newsitem.title: UK: Mechanics' error probably caused crash of WW2 plane.
newsitem.headline: Mechanics' error probably caused crash of WW2 plane.

text.p: A veteran British Mosquito fighter-bomber crashed during an air show last July probably because engineers had failed to spot a fault which severely restricted the left engine's fuel supply, investigators said on Thursday.

Both crew members were killed instantly when the 50-year-old twin-engined plane -- the last airworthy example of its kind -- dived into trees near the northwestern city of Manchester and exploded. No spectators were hurt.
The Air Accident Investigation Branch (AAIB) said in a report that the left engine's carburettor was only capable of supplying 10 percent of the fuel needed during tight manoeuvres.
The fault should have been spotted during the plane's last overhaul but for some reason the relevant test was not carried out.

The AIIB report said the limited fuel supply to the left engine was the most likely cause of the crash. It also noted some kinds of Mosquito engines were well known for momentarily cutting out during tight turns or dives.
The English-built Mosquito, largely made of wood to keep the weight down, was one of the fastest aircraft of World War Two and proved to be one of the most versatile.
